root_idea.summary: The root centers on spaciousness, breadth, and the absence of constriction.
root_idea.development: The basic sense of physical expansiveness extends to spacious places and bodily breadth, figurative openness and capacity, landscape terms, and the greeting formula مَرْحَبًا, which invokes or declares spaciousness and ease.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested greeting noun and formula.

senses.definition: To be or become spacious, ample, wide, or roomy.
senses.usage_conditions: Applied to a place or other thing. In the Quranic construction بِما رَحُبَتْ, the earth is described as spacious even while it became constricted for those concerned.

senses.definition: Welcome; a greeting or invocation expressing that someone has come to, or found, spaciousness and ease.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as the greeting formula مَرْحَبًا and, in the Quranic passages, in the negative formula لا مَرْحَبًا بِهِمْ / بِكُمْ, meaning that no welcome or spacious reception is granted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be spacious for or accommodating to someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Originally construed with بِـ, as in رَحُبَ بِكَ المَكَانُ; later usage also allowed direct transitive construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an anomalous transitive idiom, to be proper or allowable for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression أَرَحُبَكُمُ الدُّخُولُ فِي طَاعَتِهِ, concerning entry into obedience; the construction is described as exceptional.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something wide or spacious by transitive use.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the invocation رَحُبَ اللهُ جَوْفَهُ, meaning that God make his belly wide.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To welcome someone by saying مَرْحَبًا; to greet or invite someone to spaciousness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Commonly construed with بِـ, as in رَحَّبَ بِهِ, and also used for welcoming or greeting generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a thing ample, spacious, wide, or roomy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used in commands meaning “make room” or “withdraw.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become easy or open in its routes or avenues.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an affair whose ways of approach are easy although its ways of completion or return are difficult.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ample, spacious, wide, or roomy, of a place or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes a capacious cooking pot and the expression رَحَائِبُ التُّخُومِ, referring to the breadth or extent of territorial limits and regions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Physically wide in the genital region, in a specialized description of a woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical use of the adjective, distinct from ordinary spatial breadth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Broad-bellied; by extension, a great or voracious eater.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression رَحْبُ الجَوْفِ and also reported as رَحِيبٌ when used alone with this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Broad or open in breast and mind; free from distress or narrowness of mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use in the expression رَحْبُ الصَّدْرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Generous, munificent, or broad in capacity and power.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In expressions such as رَحْبُ الذِّرَاعِ and رَحْبُ البَاعِ, it may denote ability in difficulty and strength, courage, or prowess in conflict.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ampleness, spaciousness, wideness, or roominess.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an abstract noun and in invitations to advance into spaciousness or room.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A courtyard, open area, or spacious vacant portion of a mosque, house, or other place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May include an enclosure or raised platform at the entrance of a mosque; the form رَحْبَةٌ is also attested.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ample tract of land where people and herbage may gather; also a part of a valley where water flows in or collects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural رِحَابٌ can denote smooth or soft water-collecting places, including valley basins and other low or elevated tracts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where the plant ثُمَام, or panic grass, aggregates and grows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized landscape use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where grapes are dried, like a drying floor for dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The broadest rib or a broad region of the chest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer to the upper ribs near the armpits, the region where the heart beats, or related chest and flank areas; the paired form denotes corresponding ribs or flanks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A brand or mark made with a hot iron on the side of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Certain excellent she-camels associated with Arhab.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The association is variously explained as being with the Arhab tribe, a stallion, or a Yemeni place named for the tribe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in a figurative poetic expression comparing a person’s friendship with shade.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A surname or byname of ʿUrqūb, the man proverbial for lying promises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name and proverbial use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of an idol formerly worshipped in Ḥaḍramawt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name use, distinct from the greeting formula.
